- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent prices are trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after a strong upward spike in sentiment; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias correction in the 5–7 day window following sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast deviates >15% from 14-day moving average; bring forecast back toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to sentiment swings >0.5 in 3 consecutive days.
- If sentiment is high but price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment; adjust forecast downward by 3–5% to align with sentiment-to-price disconnect.
